summary.title: Space Invaders from Scratch - Part 4
summary.one_liner: You learn how to handle GLFW keyboard callbacks for player movement and firing, and how to implement bullet-alien collision and alien death in a C++ Space Invaders clone.
keywords: how to handle key press in c++ game
how to detect bullet hitting enemy
takeaways: Register a GLFW key callback with glfwSetKeyCallback and switch on key codes and actions (press/release) to change game state.
Track left/right movement with a shared direction variable so that pressing both keys cancels out, and clamp the player sprite to the game bounds.
Fire bullets on key release, store them in a fixed-size array, and remove them by overwriting with the last element when they leave the screen.
Detect bullet-alien hits with an axis-aligned rectangle overlap test, then switch the alien to a dead type shown for a fixed number of frames.
summary.summary: This fourth part of a C++ Space Invaders tutorial series adds interactivity to the game using GLFW. It starts with a key callback that quits on Esc, then adds left/right player movement through a direction counter and firing of bullets on Space release. The post also introduces alien types, a death sprite with a per-alien counter, and rectangle-based sprite overlap checks so bullets can destroy aliens. Code snippets are shown inline throughout, and the series uses only a few dependencies.
